full_judgment: 5. Plaintiff claimed that he exchanged the suit land with Nurul Ameen, who got the same by successive transferring from his predecessors and that those predecessors auction purchased the same in Certificate Case No. 24303 of 1958. The land in question appertains to C.S. plot No. 1416 of C.S. Khatian No. 67 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 64 with area of .0857 acre. The trial court on assessment of the evidence on record came to a definite finding that exhibit-1, the boinama was interpolated and over written by erasing some writings and the certified copy was also not counter signed by anybody. It was further held that the area of the land was also interpolated. Therefore, it came to a definite finding that since the plaintiff’s basis of claim of title is the auction sale, which was found as fraudulent; he failed to prove title of his predecessors. Bashiruddin and Ishaq Mia, and therefore, all subsequent transactions fall through. It further came to a definite finding that the plaintiff’s claim of payment of rent to Nurul Ameen by the tenant was also found false, as evident from the evidence Nurul Ameen P. W.2. The court of appeal below held that despite such findings regarding the forgery of certificate sale, the plaintiff could not produce any document that his predecessors got possession pursuant to such auction sale; that in the absence of delivery of possession the auction sale was not acted upon; that despite getting sufficient opportunity the plaintiff did not call for the record of the certificate sale; that against the declaration of the land as vested property, the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 33 of 1995 in which he failed to prove his title up to the High Court Division and that exhibit-1 is apparently a forged one, inasmuch as, there was cover writing in it.
